study type: Mixed methods study (secondary analysis of registry data and in-depth interviews)
exposure: Mistrust in healthcare system (language barriers, coercive authority)
cohort: The study analyzed 33,759 observations from a Global Maternal and Newborn Health Registry (2014-2016) in Chimaltenango, Guatemala, covering live births and stillbirths, and conducted 33 in-depth interviews with mothers, traditional Maya midwives, and local healthcare professionals from Indigenous Maya Kaqchikel communities.
finding: Structural social forces and healthcare system shortcomings, coupled with the resulting mistrust, increase neonatal mortality among Maya Kaqchikel communities in rural Guatemala, suggesting that collaborative relationships among healthcare staff, traditional midwives, and families could disrupt this cycle.
